newsitem.title: UK: Producer selling capping copper price - Merrill.
newsitem.headline: Producer selling capping copper price - Merrill.

text.p: A large US investment bank which took over Sumitomo copper positions is trying to push prices higher, but is meeting resistance from producers that are taking advantage of price rises to sell forward, broker Merrill Lynch said.

"Rallies above the $1,950 a tonne level basis three months LME are bringing out increasing volumes of forward selling from North and South American producers alike," said metals analyst Ted Arnold in a report.
"They are selling forward for all of 1998 and the second half of 1997. As a result, these rally attempts are increasingly failing," he added.

The unnamed bank is said to have taken over long positions from Sumitomo Corp after the Japanese giant uncovered massive losses from alleged rogue trading. The bank has undertaken to drive prices higher ahead of options declarations to spark delta hedging, and by drawing down LME stocks, Arnold said.
But prices have had trouble maintaining a stance above $1,970.

"The investment bank that is currently doing the squeezing simply does not have the resources that Sumitomo had to squeeze with nor does the bank have all the associates that Sumitomo had to squeeze with," the report said.
Producers are well-advised to lock in higher prices, since the fundamentals are rapidly pushing the market into surplus, Arnold said.
"Metal is progressively less and less tight. Selling forward into strong price rallies makes very good sense for producers and merchants," he said.
